analyses.key_finding: Need-related packages systematically more active (82.93% vs 57.50%, p=0.00157). Wilson CI95 lower bound 0.6874 > 0.6. All gates met.
analyses.platform_char: PyPI JSON API provides activity metadata: release count, project URLs, classifiers, development status
analyses.classification_rubric: active: activity_score >= 10 (version presence + homepage URL + documentation URL + source URL + Development Status classifier 5 + Development Status classifier 4)

analyses.key_finding: Need-related packages 100% active vs random 0%. G1: 10/10 need-related harvested. G2: arm A mean=8.9, arm B mean=0.0, t=66.0 p≪0.001. G3: 10/10 need-related active, Wilson CI95 LB=0.7225 > 0.6.
analyses.platform_char: NPM JSON API provides activity metadata: release presence, homepage URL, repository URL, Keywords
analyses.classification_rubric: active: activity_score >= 5 (release presence + homepage URL + repository URL + Keywords)

analyses.key_finding: Need-related median 7.8M downloads vs random 195K (~40×). G1-G4 all pass. Effect size: need-related packages have ~40× higher downloads.
analyses.platform_char: NuGet Azure Search API provides totalDownloads field (cumulative downloads across all versions)
analyses.classification_rubric: Need-related: tags/description/title contain developer problem-solving keywords

analyses.key_finding: G2 FAIL: both need-related and random repos have 100% active rate by stars; median stars 57,218 vs 60,770 (Mann-Whitney p=0.79), no significant difference in popularity. The principle requires a varying activity metric, not a uniform popularity one.
analyses.platform_char: GitHub stars do NOT systematically differentiate need-related from random repos; the platform's popularity metric is confounded by network effects, prior fame, and repository visibility
analyses.classification_rubric: N/A - star-based activity not correlated with need-relatedness

analyses.key_finding: G1 FAIL (could not reach n≥30 per arm), G2 FAIL, G4 PASS (100% have recent_downloads > 0) — all crates active eliminates binary discrimination. Need-related vs random cannot be distinguished by download activity alone.
analyses.platform_char: crates.io: all packages have recent_downloads > 0 (100% active), eliminating the binary differentiation that the view-count principle relies on. Need-related vs random cannot be distinguished by download activity alone.

analyses.key_finding: G3 FAIL: activity-rate difference 7.8pp fails 10pp threshold; G4 FAIL: arrival-field rate only 53.6% (below 95% threshold). Principle does not generalize to Maven Central POM metadata.
analyses.platform_char: Maven Central: POM metadata activity-rate difference between need-related and random packages is not significant (7.8pp, below 10pp gate). Arrival field (totalDownloads) present in only 53.6% of packages, below the 95% threshold.

analyses.key_finding: G2 FAIL: p=0.089 not significant; G3 FAIL: Wilson LB=0.089 far below 0.60 threshold. View-count principle does not generalize to ML model registry — download dynamics differ from code package registries, signal too weak.
analyses.platform_char: Hugging Face Hub: both need-related and random models have low active rates (12.4% vs 8.6%), download dynamics differ from code package repositories. The differentiation signal is too weak.

summary.key_characteristic: Package repository with exposable activity metadata
summary.effect_size_range: NPM: 100% vs 0% (near-perfect) to NuGet: ~40× download ratio

boundary_reasoning.works: Package repos expose metadata about independent arrivals (releases, downloads, URLs, keywords)
boundary_reasoning.fails-insignificant-diff: Activity-rate difference below gate threshold (Maven Central: 7.8pp < 10pp)
boundary_reasoning.fails-signal-weak: Both categories have low similar active rates (Hugging Face: 12.4% vs 8.6%)
boundary_reasoning.fails-uniform-metric: Uniform popularity metric not correlated with need-relatedness (GitHub stars)
